source_caption:
To perfectly capture the deeply unsettling, deeply enigmatic presence of the film’s terrifying antagonist Aunt Gladys, director Zach Cregger deliberately avoided using traditional, heavy horror movie monster tropes. Instead, he completely submerged Amy Madigan in the “uncanny valley” by using subtle, highly specific prosthetics that made her face look just slightly asymmetrical. Drawing heavy visual inspiration from the fiercely bizarre photography of Cindy Sherman, the makeup team gave Madigan a slightly off-kilter nose, elongated earlobes, “nubbins” for teeth, and had her wear only a single contact lens. By refusing to bury his villain under a mountain of rubber, Cregger masterfully proves that the most viscerally disturbing cinematic monsters are the ones who look almost entirely human—a brilliant choice that ultimately led to Madigan winning the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

Weapons (2025), directed by Zach Cregger, starring Josh Brolin, Julia Garner, Amy Madigan. When an entire third-grade classroom of seventeen children mysteriously vanishes in the dead of night, a deeply panicked, heavily desperate small town slowly discovers that a highly enigmatic, deeply supernatural witch disguised as an eccentric elderly woman is violently manipulating the adults and draining the children’s life force to sustain her own terrifying immortality.

source_details.synopsis: Weapons is a 2025 American supernatural mystery horror film directed, written, produced, and co-scored by Zach Cregger. It stars an ensemble cast including Josh Brolin, Julia Garner, Alden Ehrenreich, Austin Abrams, Cary Christopher, Toby Huss, Benedict Wong, and Amy Madigan. Its plot follows the case of seventeen children from the same classroom who mysteriously run away on the same night at the same time. After the critical and commercial success of his film Barbarian (2022), Cregger began working on the spec script for Weapons.
